title: Capsule CRM Review (2026)
intro: Capsule is a simple CRM for small businesses focused on contacts, sales pipelines, tasks, and lightweight automation. This review covers Free through Ultimate pricing, capabilities, limitations, and alternatives.
summary: Capsule is a strong affordable CRM for SMBs. Free and Starter are easy on-ramps; Growth is the practical automation tier. Scores reflect first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
verdict: Capsule is a strong simple CRM for small businesses that want contacts, pipelines, and light automation without suite complexity. Free and Starter make onboarding affordable; Growth is the practical plan when automations and advanced reporting matter. This review is based on first-party product, pricing, and Capsule blog research — not hands-on product testing.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Capsule’s product story is simplicity for SMB teams — contacts, pipelines, and tasks without enterprise CRM ceremony.
Solid sales pipelines with plan-scaled pipeline counts; strong enough for SMB selling, not positioned as the deepest pipeline CRM.
Workflow automations arrive at Growth and are a meaningful step up from Starter, without becoming a marketing-automation suite.
Gmail/Outlook add-ins, templates, and shared mailbox cover SMB sales email needs; not a campaign platform.
Basic reporting on lower paid tiers and advanced reporting from Growth match typical SMB manager needs.
Custom fields and pipelines scale by plan; Ultimate unlocks unlimited fields for larger SMBs.
Common SMB connectors (email, accounting, Zapier-style) are documented; breadth is practical rather than marketplace-maximal.
Lightweight administration is part of the value proposition for small teams, especially on Free/Starter defaults.
Advanced/Ultimate raise caps for larger SMBs, but Capsule remains an SMB CRM rather than mid-market enterprise platform.
Free plan plus $18 Starter annual pricing is among the clearer value stories in SMB CRM.

faq.question: How much does Capsule CRM cost?
faq.answer: Capsule publishes Free ($0), Starter ($18), Growth ($36), Advanced ($54), and Ultimate ($72) per user per month when billed annually (USD). Paid plans include a 14-day trial. Confirm current pricing on Capsule’s site.

faq.question: Does Capsule have a free plan?
faq.answer: Yes. Capsule’s Free plan supports up to two users with limited contacts/pipelines.

faq.question: Which Capsule plan includes automations?
faq.answer: Workflow automations are documented from the Growth plan upward.

faq.question: Is this a hands-on SoftwareGlimpse lab review?
faq.answer: No. This review is approved based on first-party Capsule pricing/product/blog research, not hands-on testing.

sections.heading: What Capsule is
sections.body: Capsule is a simple CRM for small businesses. It focuses on contacts, pipelines, tasks, and projects rather than heavy marketing suites.

sections.heading: Pricing and plans
sections.body: Capsule’s ladder runs Free → Starter → Growth → Advanced → Ultimate. Annual USD list pricing starts at $18/user/mo for Starter and tops out at $72 for Ultimate.

sections.heading: Core CRM capabilities
sections.body: Documented strengths include contact management, pipelines, tasks/projects, Growth+ automations, email add-ins, AI assist, and mobile apps.

sections.heading: Who it’s for
sections.body: Best for SMBs wanting affordable simple CRM. Less ideal for marketing automation or enterprise governance needs.

productExperience.summary: Based on Capsule’s documented workflow, teams manage contacts, track opportunities on pipelines, organize tasks/projects, automate from Growth, and use AI assist for content — with mobile access for on-the-go updates.
